pure-announcement.rationale: It is release coverage but explains a transferable architecture trade-off: containers share the host kernel while full VMs boot too slowly for RL rollouts, and snapshot-plus-fork microVMs dissolve that trade.

duplicate.rationale: The automated-w2s-sandbox concept is a research-problem environment with an evaluation API, not microVM isolation infrastructure for RL rollouts, and no other nearest concept is closer.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The MIT-licensed repo and documentation are linked, so the architecture and figures can be checked at the source.

durability.rationale: The note leans on vendor-reported v0 specifics — sub-50 ms resume, a 16-child fork cap, kernel 6.8+/Ubuntu 24.04 prerequisites, a control plane documented as prototype — that will drift, even though the fork-amortizes-setup pattern endures.

actionability.rationale: Its concrete steps are AgentENV deployment paths; the decision-level guidance for anyone building agentic RL infrastructure (choose microVM fork over container pools, keep E2B API compatibility) stays at a paragraph of framing.

atomicity.rationale: The whole note serves one statable idea: make kernel-level isolation cheap enough for RL training scale via incrementally snapshotted, forkable Firecracker microVMs.
